subject.title: [Bug]: gateway.nodes.denyCommands silently accepts invalid command names without warning

question: Should `gateway.nodes.denyCommands` validation at config write time warn only, fail closed for unknown names, or remain audit-only for custom/plugin command compatibility?
rationale: The source bug is clear, but changing config-write behavior on a security-sensitive allow/deny surface affects custom/plugin command IDs and operator workflows, so automation should not choose the policy unilaterally.

options.title: Warn on unknown names
options.body: Reuse the security audit command catalog and suggestions during `openclaw config set/patch` while still allowing custom or plugin commands to be saved.

options.title: Fail closed on unknown names
options.body: Reject unknown denylist entries during config writes and require a separate explicit story for custom commands.

options.title: Keep audit-only
options.body: Leave config writes permissive and rely on `openclaw security audit` to diagnose ineffective denylist entries after the fact.

recommendation.title: Warn on unknown names
recommendation.body: Reuse the security audit command catalog and suggestions during `openclaw config set/patch` while still allowing custom or plugin commands to be saved.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter's recent security-audit hardening work is the strongest routing signal for choosing how this audit warning should move into config writes.
